text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Chairman of the ruling Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party, Ceslovas Jursenas, predicted the party would win at least 30 seats in the October 20 parliamentary elections. The party currently has 30 seats.

- Lithuanian Homeland Union introduced its list of 120 candidates ahead of the October parliament elections. The list was headed by present opposition leader Vytautas Landsbergis, former Finance Minister Elvyra Kuneviciene and former Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnoris.
- The U.S.-Iraq military conflict boosted prices on Lithuania's oil market.
- The Lithuanian Christian Democrats' election programme approved on Saturday calls for a 'social economy'.
- Respublika publishes an extended investigative article about the growing use of synthetic narcotics such as LSD and Ecstasy in Lithuania.
